correctness.rationale: Frobenius-equivariant odd theta/bitangent correspondence identifies the 28 lines with odd refinements of a six-dimensional binary symplectic form. Two independently implemented full-group enumerations, one in the 28-permutation action and one in the six-by-six symplectic matrix action, both reach 1,451,520 elements and independently recover identical 25 cycle partitions and the five minimum-orbit histogram. The transvections have symplectic origin and generate a group of full known Sp6(2) order. A separate F29 verifier exhausts its 871 projective lines and gives explicit polynomial-square identities for 28 rational bitangents of the smooth Klein quartic. The coordinate change with beta^7=2 identifies the proposed sharp curve with Klein over F29^7, and Frobenius acts by three distinct seventh-root diagonal eigenvalues: no proper power fixes any bitangent, as the three coordinate lines are not bitangents. The last step is a proof over the algebraic closure, not a finite sample. The proof distinguishes least degree from common splitting degree.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the five-value classification of the smallest extension degree of a geometric bitangent line for all smooth plane quartics over odd finite fields, together with the explicit degree-seven sharpness example X^3Y+2Y^3Z+Z^3X over F29 and its four exact degree-seven orbits. The theta correspondence, 28-point Sp6(2) representation, Klein automorphisms and twist framework are prior art. Meagher--Top §8 covers twists and Jacobian traces but does not establish the evaluated bitangent field-degree bound and the concrete example. Dalla Piazza--Fiorentino--Salvati Manni covers bitangent structures, not the field-degree theorem. Standard 28-point permutation data may make the abstract bound derivable, so historical priority is explicitly qualified; one 2008 dissertation was catalogued but its full PDF could not be accessed. The literature and mathematical-record searches identified no directly covering evaluated theorem.
residual_risks: The Sp6(2) minimum-orbit classification may be reconstructible from published 28-point permutation tables, reducing the novelty of the group-only ingredient.
Order-seven Klein twists are classical; historical literature may already record the bitangent Galois orbit implication, even if the inspected 2010 primary manuscript does not.
Full text of the 2008 thesis was not accessible; no negative coverage claim is made about that document.
The identified novelty does not imply every abstract cycle spectrum is geometrically realized over each finite field.

value.rationale: Field extension degrees of bitangent lines and odd theta characteristics are natural algorithmic and arithmetic invariants of nonhyperelliptic genus-three curves. The sharp bound 7, exact list of possible minimal degrees, and an explicit curve requiring degree 7 provide a complete natural optimality statement. The concrete arithmetic obstruction is not merely a numerical recomputation of a known table; the Kummer Frobenius argument certifies why all 28 bitangents remain nonrational up to degree 6. The theorem excludes unsupported general moduli realization claims, and its utility does not require a downstream result.
